top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) is new chemistry requiring ligand design to overcome slow C-N reductive elimination and beta-hydride elimination, is general and used daily at industrial scale, has been reproduced for over 25 years, and has a clean two-person attribution. The 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi tin-amide precedent are manageable through citation wording. Targeted protein degradation (P001) is the strongest alternative but is still unapproved clinically and joins two historically distinct strands; ionizable lipid nanoparticles are mature but have unsettled attribution and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize; base editing is too young.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am the only synthetic organic chemist on the committee, so I have a field bias toward a synthetic methodology
